answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake reputation earned in a grove of long-lived, mutually audited work histories rather than a single sign-up. Every job leaves a verifiable pulse of completed work, payments, and peer ratings that a newcomer cannot fake overnight. Adding a pigment test — a small, time-locked deposit that is slashed when an identity is caught duplicating work — makes spawning a thousand fake agents cost a thousand deposits, so attackers pay real money for every fake voice while honest agents keep their stake.
